knowledge_point.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The first equation is a false statement. Hence, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ 5 \\ -10\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ 5 \\ -10\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ 5 \\ -10\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ 5 \\ -10\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-10\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=0$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ {x}_{1}-(0) &=-5 \\ {x}_{1} &=-5 \\ {x}_{1} &=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-5$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-10 \\ 2(-5)+3(0) &=-10 \\ -10 &=-10\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-5$ and ${x}_{2}=0$, which means

$$
-5{a}_{1}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-5)+(0)=-5.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 10 \\ 14\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 10 \\ 14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 10 \\ 14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 10 \\ 14\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-18 \\ 2{x}_{1} &=10 \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{1}=5$.

Substituting ${x}_{1}=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-18 \\ -4(5)+{x}_{2} &=-18 \\ {x}_{2} &=2 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=14 \\ (5)+4(2) &=14 \\ 13 &=14\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=5$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=0 \\ (5)-{x}_{2} &=0 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ {x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=5$, which means

$$
5{c}_{1}+5{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(5)+(5)=10.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} &=-8 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=-1$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=1 \\ 4(-1)+{x}_{2} &=1 \\ {x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=8 \\ (-1)+2(5) &=8 \\ 9 &=8\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
